title: The Drucker Forum's 'India Way' workshop builds on the book — 50 family business owners asked what a company is for
summary: Guptara chaired the workshop, the third edition of The India Way at the Global Peter Drucker Forum, held in the Hofburg in Vienna and facilitated by the LivingMachine Institute. Mark Goyder, who founded Tomorrow's Company in 1996, opened with Japanese firms that have lasted three centuries and more, then turned to Incorruptible for how governance holds a mission in place.
blockquote: Mark then drew on Eric Ries' new book "Incorruptible", which explores why even companies founded with the best intentions can drift away from their purpose, and how governance can protect their mission over time.

source_urls.label: Mark Goyder (Founder, Tomorrow's Company), the workshop's opening speaker, on learning 'from the mistakes of the West, and from #Incorruptible'

The Drucker Forum's own pre-events programme billing the session: 'Mark Goyder brings this formidable experience to interpreting Eric Ries’ Incorruptible and its convergence with the LivingMachine Institute’s practices on Institutional Longevity Value.'
